clue.text: Like the Tiger master's wife among the beefeaters ?

definitions.text: Like the Tiger master's wife among the beefeaters ?

parts.words: Like the Tiger master's wife among the beefeaters
parts.note: in Macbeth a witch insults the sailor's wife (her husband is master of the ship Tiger) by calling her fed on the best cuts of beef, the haunch kind that beefeaters would enjoy

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a ship captain's wife compares with the guards at the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth the First Witch calls the wife of the master of the Tiger a 'rump-fed ronyon'; beefeaters (Tower of London guards) suggest people fed on beef rump.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's witch uses this compound as an insult meaning pampered and fat from eating choice joints of beef.

clue.text: Heathen god of a Border Scotsman

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A pagan deity said to belong to a man from the Scottish Borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is the region of Scotland next to England, which the surface uses; here 'Border' is just an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament this was a Syrian deity worshipped in Damascus, a pagan idol in biblical terms.

clue.text: A piece of music in greater degree, as they say

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the words are to be pronounced and matched by sound

parts.note: more so means to a greater degree

explanation.surface: A description of a composition that is even more so, in common parlance.
explanation.walkthrough: French for a piece or morsel, used in English for a short musical composition, sounds like 'more so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French for a bit or morsel, it names a short composition or extract.

clue.text: The way he talks, he'll never get there

definitions.text: The way he talks, he'll never get there

parts.words: The way he talks, he'll never get there
parts.note: the saying that this kind of talk will get you nowhere

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a man whose speech shows he will never succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'flattery will get you nowhere' is behind it: the one who talks that way never arrives anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who pays insincere compliments is, by the proverb, someone whose smooth words get nowhere.

clue.text: Record-holder for an under-ground beauty spot?

definitions.text: Record-holder for an under-ground beauty spot?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the underworld itself
a patch was a small piece of black silk worn on the face as a beauty spot
a box holds papers and records

explanation.surface: A question about a container for papers at a lovely place below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says this is the box holding the papers for Dis's patch; in the Commons it is the box on the table that ministers speak from.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for official documents, and in the House of Commons the box at which front-bench members stand.

clue.text: One bird separates the cream…

definitions.meaning: a seabird that flies low over water, scooping fish with its long lower bill
a perforated ladle used to lift cream off milk does this job

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb to skim: the bird skims the waves, the ladle skims milk for its top layer.

clue.text: No Madam, this car is for the government

annotationWithheld.why: 'No Madam, this car is for the government' (3), as the scan prints it: 'No Madam' gives SIR, but no reading found makes 'this car is for the government' give or define SIR
annotationWithheld.clue: No Madam, this car is for the government

clue.text: Contribution gratefully received by computer ?

parts.note: a gift to a charity is the surface; really data fed into a machine, also any contribution

explanation.surface: A thank-you note for a donation, apparently sent by a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a charity donation; the word means a contribution of ideas or effort and also the data a computer takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a contribution of effort or ideas and, in computing, the data fed into a system.

clue.text: No man born of woman won him his crown

definitions.text: No man born of woman won him his crown

parts.words: No man born of woman won him his crown
parts.note: in Macbeth, Macduff, not born of woman, kills the tyrant and the dead King Duncan's son is crowned

explanation.surface: A line about a king who owed his throne to a man not born of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The witches tell Macbeth no man of woman born can harm him; Macduff, born by Caesarean, kills him, and Duncan's son takes the crown. The clue's 'No man' is Macduff.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan's elder son becomes King of Scotland at the close of Shakespeare's Macbeth.

clue.text: Make new estimate of the old thing about Euclidean bridge types

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other here

parts.note: res is Latin, the ancient language, for thing
the pons asinorum, bridge of asses, is a theorem in Euclid, so donkeys are its kind

explanation.surface: Someone revalues an antique while thinking about geometry and card players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ASSES inside RES. 'Bridge types' wants to mean card players; Euclid's fifth proposition is nicknamed the bridge of asses because slow pupils stumble on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise something again, revising an earlier judgement.

clue.text: … while another has the answer in combination

indicators.note: the abbreviation for answer sits inside the word for a combination

parts.note: a merger is a combination of two firms
ANS is a standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a second bird is said to hold the solution in a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 5 across: 'another' means another bird, the previous clue having defined a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander and its relatives are fish-eating diving ducks, so this is another bird after the skimmer.

clue.text: Dance jacket, on the dot

definitions.meaning: a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-time
a short knitted jacket for women was named after the dance
the name goes before 'dot' for a pattern of regular large spots

explanation.definitionFit: The dance craze of the 1840s lent its name to a fashionable short jacket and to a spotted fabric pattern.

clue.text: Higher notes for such ones, it's plain to see

indicators.note: the clue says that this kind of ones makes the higher notes, so the word ones is stripped away to leave the kind

parts.note: overtones are the higher harmonics sounding above a fundamental note
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical remark about high pitches, ending with an observation that something is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: Higher notes are OVERTONES, which split as OVERT + ONES: the clue asks what kind of 'ones' they are, and removing ONES leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly and not concealed is plain for anyone to see.

clue.text: Next-to-Olympian rites involving some flannel ?

parts.note: cleanliness is next to godliness, so washing is next to the gods of Olympus, and a face flannel is the cloth used for it

explanation.surface: Ceremonies just below the gods of Olympus, conducted with a little smooth talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'cleanliness is next to godliness' makes washing 'next to Olympian'; a flannel is a British face cloth, and 'flannel' also means evasive talk, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal or humorous term for the act of washing oneself, often treated as a ritual.

clue.text: Tradesman Gilpin, crazy ride planner

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper called Gilpin plans an outlandish journey on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: In William Cowper's comic poem, John Gilpin is a London cloth merchant whose horse bolts with him. 'crazy' rearranges RIDE PLANNER.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gilpin in Cowper's ballad was a merchant selling cloth and household textiles.

clue.text: Wartime aircraft lights still used in blackouts

definitions.text: Wartime aircraft lights still used in blackouts

parts.note: the Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter plane of the Second World War
lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Lighting named after a fighter plane that people still reach for when the power fails.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: these storm-proof paraffin lanterns share a name with the wartime fighter and are still lit during power cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-chimneyed paraffin lanterns that stay lit in wind are kept for power cuts.

clue.text: Times of scarcity won't worry Mr Sprat

definitions.text: Times of scarcity won't worry Mr Sprat

parts.words: Times of scarcity won't worry Mr Sprat
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Jack Sprat could eat no fat, so meagre periods suit him

explanation.surface: A comment that famine would not trouble a man who dislikes fatty food.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat 'could eat no fat', so thin times would suit him.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard periods when food and money run short, like the seven thin cows of Pharaoh's dream.

clue.text: How to avoid waste in employment to some purpose ?

definitions.text: How to avoid waste in employment
definitions.meaning: split as two words, it tells you to employ something completely
in a way that serves a good end

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to employ something completely; as one it means helpfully, to good effect.

clue.text: No shortage of extra play- ers, it seems

definitions.text: No shortage of extra play- ers, it seems

parts.words: No shortage of extra play- ers, it seems
parts.note: a super is an extra in a stage crowd, so plenty of supers looks like a description of the word for great excess

explanation.surface: A theatre producer has plenty of walk-on actors to choose from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supers' (supernumeraries) are extras on stage; read as SUPER + ABUNDANCE, the word seems to mean a crowd of them, while it really means a great excess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a quantity far greater than needed, an excess well past mere plenty.

clue.text: You would do well to name Carmen's author

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to thrive or succeed
... Mérimée wrote the novella on which Bizet's opera is based

explanation.definitionFit: To flourish and succeed, and also the first name of Mérimée, who wrote the novella behind the opera.

clue.text: An astonishing type of warning

definitions.meaning: a ..., in informal speech, is a person who is amazing or outrageous

explanation.definitionFit: A cautionary word is an admonition, and colloquially someone remarkable is called 'a real one'.

clue.text: Stones a Turkish commander set up

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word set is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer arranges some gems.
explanation.definitionFit: These banded forms of chalcedony are semi-precious gems.

clue.text: Mechanical kitchen vessel converted from oxide

indicators.note: something converted is changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry claim that a kitchen gadget was made by transforming a metal oxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges the nine letters of FROM OXIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric blender or mixing machine with a bowl is a powered kitchen container for beating ingredients.

clue.text: Delicious food, up-country style

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so the country name is reversed

parts.note: Annam was a kingdom in what is now central Vietnam

explanation.surface: A description of rich rural cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-country' suggests the countryside, but 'up' reverses ANNAM, an old Indochinese kingdom; 'style' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The miraculous bread from heaven in Exodus, hence any delightful and unexpected food.

clue.text: No older than a Mormon leader

definitions.meaning: describing someone of few years, not past the age of youth
Brigham ... led the Mormons to Utah

explanation.definitionFit: Youthful means not old, and Brigham, the second president of the Latter-day Saints, carried this surname.

clue.text: Booked an almost wolf-like French criminal

indicators.note: almost means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: lupine means like a wolf

explanation.surface: Someone reserved a rather wolfish crook from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' hints that the criminal lives in books: Arsène Lupin is Maurice Leblanc's fictional gentleman thief. 'almost' drops the last letter of LUPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsène is the gentleman burglar of Maurice Leblanc's stories, the best-known crook of French fiction.

clue.text: Clipper bringing peacocks etc, to your garden

definitions.text: Clipper bringing peacocks etc, to your garden

parts.words: Clipper bringing peacocks etc, to your garden
parts.note: a fast sailing ship bringing exotic birds is the surface; really a gardener clips hedges into bird shapes

explanation.surface: A fast sailing ship delivers exotic birds to the reader's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' suggests a tea clipper importing birds, but it means a person with shears who trims yew and box into peacocks and other shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: This gardener shapes shrubs ornamentally by cutting, often into birds and animals.

clue.text: Bell-boy

definitions.meaning: Great ... is the famous bell of Christ Church, Oxford
a male animal, especially a cat

explanation.definitionFit: Great Tom is the Oxford bell, and tom also names a male, as in a tomcat.

clue.text: The long one of the law for sailing-ships ?

definitions.text: The long one of the law for sailing-ships ?

parts.words: The long one of the law for sailing-ships
parts.note: the long arm of the law, with arm given a nautical counterpart on a ship's mast

explanation.surface: A question about what plays the role of police reach on old sailing vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'the long arm of the law' gives ARM; on a sailing ship the long spar crossing the mast has an arm at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar slung across a mast to carry a square sail has outer ends called by this name, and pirates were hanged from it.

clue.text: Revolts follow alarms

definitions.meaning: getting out of bed happens after the alarm clock rings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means rebellions and also the acts of getting up from bed, which come after the clock rings.
